## Purpose

This SOP describes procedures for characterizing the physical habitat
of wadeable streams using the quantitative transect-based protocol
developed by the California State Water Resources Control Board's
Surface Water Ambient Monitoring Program (SWAMP). Physical habitat data
document the structural condition of streams -- channel dimensions,
substrate composition, bank stability, riparian vegetation, instream
cover, and human influence -- and are essential for interpreting
bioassessment results and diagnosing the causes of biological
impairment [@ode2016; @barbour1999].

The protocol produces data compatible with the California Index of
Physical-habitat Integrity (IPI), the California Stream Condition
Index (CSCI), and the Algal Stream Condition Index (ASCI), enabling
direct comparison with statewide reference data [@rehn2017; @mazor2016].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Wadeable perennial and intermittent streams and
  rivers where personnel can safely wade (generally depths less than
  approximately 1 m and velocities less than approximately 1.2 m/s)
- **Does not apply to:** Non-wadeable rivers requiring boat-based
  protocols; estuarine or tidal reaches; depressional wetlands (use
  CRAM instead); lake or reservoir shorelines
- **Location:** All EA Program stream monitoring sites, including
  tributaries to the Santa Ana River watershed and other southern
  California waterbodies


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Project Lead | Approve site selection and sampling design              |
| Field Lead        | Coordinate logistics, lead reach delineation, verify equipment |
| Trained Personnel | Collect physical habitat data per this SOP              |
| New Students      | Complete training before participating in field crews   |


## Definitions

- **b-axis (intermediate axis):** The intermediate dimension of a
  sediment particle (not the longest or shortest axis); the standard
  measurement used to classify particle size in pebble counts; measured
  with a metric ruler to the nearest mm [@ode2016].
- **Bankfull channel:** The stage at which water just begins to
  overflow the channel banks into the floodplain; the reference
  condition for channel geometry measurements in SWAMP; typically
  evidenced by a change in bank slope, a break in vegetation, or the
  top of the point bar [@ode2016; @peck2006].
- **Cobble embeddedness:** The percentage of the surface area of
  gravel, cobble, and boulder particles that is surrounded and buried
  by fine sediment (sand, silt, clay); an indicator of fine sediment
  loading and hyporheic connectivity [@ode2016].
- **CPOM (coarse particulate organic matter):** Organic material
  (leaves, needles, twigs, bark) with a largest dimension between 1 mm
  and 10 cm; recorded at substrate measurement points as an indicator
  of allochthonous organic input to the stream.
- **D16, D50, D84:** Percentile statistics of the particle-size
  distribution from a pebble count; the particle size at which 16%,
  50%, or 84% of particles are smaller; used to characterize substrate
  texture; D50 is the median particle diameter.
- **Embeddedness:** See cobble embeddedness.
- **IPI (Index of Physical-habitat Integrity):** The California
  statewide index of stream physical condition calculated from SWAMP
  physical habitat data; scores from 0 (most disturbed) to 1 (least
  disturbed); used alongside the CSCI for reach-level condition
  assessment [@rehn2017].
- **Inter-transect:** A transect located halfway between two main
  transects; used for substrate, embeddedness, and organic matter
  measurements but not for cross-section geometry; see Appendix B for
  inter-transect locations [@ode2016].
- **Main transect:** One of 11 equally spaced transects (A through K)
  across the full sampling reach; the primary sampling unit for all
  SWAMP physical habitat modules including cross-section geometry,
  bankfull identification, substrate, canopy cover, bank stability,
  human influence, and riparian vegetation.
- **OHW (ordinary high-water mark):** The line on the bank formed by
  the action of water in its ordinary course; used as an alternative
  bankfull indicator where clear geomorphic evidence is absent.
- **Pebble count:** A randomized survey of substrate particle sizes
  at systematically distributed points along transects; each particle
  is measured at the toe of the measurer's boot or wading rod tip to
  ensure objectivity; produces the particle-size distribution used to
  calculate IPI substrate metrics [@ode2016; @peck2006].
- **Reach:** A representative stream segment typically 150 m in length
  (or 37.5× the mean wetted width for wider streams), within which
  all SWAMP physical habitat measurements are collected; selected to
  encompass representative channel features and minimize confounding
  influences of point sources or major confluences [@ode2016].
- **Riparian zone:** The terrestrial area adjacent to the stream
  channel that is influenced by periodic flooding and that contributes
  organic material, shade, and bank stability to the aquatic system;
  assessed in SWAMP modules I (riparian vegetation) and G (bank
  stability).
- **Sinuosity:** The ratio of the actual stream channel length to
  the straight-line valley length over the reach; values greater than
  1.5 indicate a meandering channel; a component of the SWAMP reach
  characterization.
- **Thalweg:** The line of deepest flow along the channel axis;
  followed during the longitudinal profile module to characterize
  channel bed elevation changes.
- **Wetted width:** The horizontal distance across the stream from
  water's edge to water's edge at a transect; used to determine reach
  length (37.5× mean wetted width) and to scale substrate sampling
  interval.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Drowning and swift water:** Do not wade in flows deeper than
  approximately waist height or where footing is unstable. Always
  face upstream. Use a wading rod for support.
- **Slippery substrates:** Algae-covered cobble and bedrock are
  extremely slippery. Wear felt-soled or studded wading boots.
- **Biological:** Waterborne pathogens, poison oak, ticks, snakes,
  and stinging insects. Check for ticks after every field day.
- **Heat:** Southern California field sites can exceed 40 °C during
  summer. Carry adequate water and take shade breaks.
- **Sensitive species:** California red-legged frog, arroyo toad,
  southwestern willow flycatcher, and steelhead may be present at
  some sites. Consult permit requirements before sampling (see
  [SOP-F004](SOP-F004-site-access-permits.qmd)).
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Chest or hip waders (neoprene or breathable)
- [ ] Wading boots with felt or studded soles
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen, long sleeves)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling samples)

### Permits

Sampling in or near habitat for listed species may require a CDFW
Scientific Collecting Permit and/or a USFWS Section 10 permit. The PI
must confirm permit status before fieldwork at any new site.

### Invasive Species Prevention

Decontaminate all wading gear between sites per
[SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd).

### Emergency Procedures

A minimum of two people must be present for any in-stream work. Refer
to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Fiberglass measuring tape (50 m)      | For establishing transect tag lines      |
| Surveyor's rod or stadia rod          | For measuring depth at cross-sections    |
| Metric ruler (30 cm, mm gradations)   | For pebble count (b-axis measurement)    |
| Convex spherical densiometer          | For canopy cover measurements            |
| Clinometer (Suunto or equivalent)     | For channel slope                        |
| Compass                               | For bearing and sinuosity                |
| GPS unit or smartphone                | For recording coordinates at each transect |
| Wading rod                            | For support and depth reference          |
| SWAMP Physical Habitat Field Data Sheets | See Appendix A; print on waterproof paper |
| Clipboard and mechanical pencils      |                                          |
| Camera (waterproof or in dry bag)     | Photo-document each transect             |
| Flagging tape                         | For marking transect locations           |


## Estimated Time

| Task                                  | Time (2-person crew)                     |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Reach delineation and transect setup  | 20--30 minutes                           |
| Full physical habitat assessment (Modules C--M) | 1.5--2.5 hours                |
| Slope and sinuosity (Module L)        | 20--40 minutes                           |
| Photographs (Module M)                | 10--15 minutes                           |
| Total                                 | 2--3.5 hours per reach                   |


## Procedure

### Reach Delineation

The sampling reach defines the stream segment over which all
measurements are collected [@ode2016].

1. Select a representative reach of appropriate length (150 m for
   streams with mean wetted width ≤ 10 m; 250 m for wider streams).
2. Walk the reach before beginning measurements to identify the
   thalweg, bankfull indicators, and any safety hazards.
3. Mark the downstream boundary (Transect A) and record GPS
   coordinates.
4. Stretch the measuring tape upstream along the thalweg (not the
   bank) to the upstream boundary (Transect K).
5. Set transect locations at equal intervals (e.g., every 15 m for a
   150 m reach), placing chaining pins or flagging at each transect.

::: {.callout-tip}
Select reaches that are representative of the stream segment. Avoid
reaches with immediate upstream or downstream disturbances (bridges,
dam tailwaters, outfalls) unless those features are the sampling
target [@ode2016].
:::

### Module A: Reach-Level Information

Record at the start of each visit:

- GPS coordinates at Transects A (downstream) and K (upstream)
- Date, time, crew members
- General weather and flow conditions (normal, high, low, dry)
- Any unusual conditions (algal blooms, trash accumulation, visible
  pollutants, recent disturbance)

### Module B: Bankfull Identification Calibration

Before beginning measurements, the full crew must agree on bankfull
indicators [@ode2016]:

1. Identify at least two independent lines of evidence for bankfull
   (e.g., break in bank slope, top of point bar, change in vegetation,
   flood debris line).
2. Walk the first 2--3 transects together and calibrate agreement on
   bankfull height.
3. Differences in bankfull identification between crew members are the
   largest source of inter-observer variability in SWAMP physical
   habitat data.

### Module C: Cross-Section Geometry (Main Transects)

At each main transect (A through K) [@ode2016; @peck2006]:

1. Stretch the measuring tape across the channel from left to right
   bank at the bankfull boundary (looking downstream).
2. Record the total bankfull width to the nearest 0.1 m.
3. Record the wetted width to the nearest 0.1 m.
4. At 5 equally spaced points across the wetted channel, measure water
   depth to the nearest cm using the surveyor's rod.
5. Record the thalweg depth (deepest point).
6. Estimate the dominant bank angle (undercut, vertical, steep,
   gradual, flat) for left and right banks.

### Module D: Substrate (Pebble Count)

At each of the 21 transects (main and inter-transects), at 5 equally
spaced points across the wetted channel [@ode2016]:

1. Measure **water depth** to the nearest cm.
2. Pick up the particle at the toe of your boot (or wading rod tip)
   and measure the **b-axis** to the nearest mm. Record on the field
   form.
3. If the particle cannot be picked up (bedrock, hardpan), record the
   appropriate size class code (see Appendix C).
4. Record presence or absence of **CPOM** at each point.

This produces 105 substrate measurements per reach.

### Module E: Cobble Embeddedness

At each substrate measurement point on main transects, if the particle
is gravel, cobble, or boulder:

1. Estimate the **percentage of the particle surface buried** by fine
   sediment to the nearest 5% or 10%.
2. Record sand and finer substrate as 100% embedded by convention.
3. Do not assess embeddedness for bedrock.

### Module F: Algal and Macrophyte Cover

At each of the five substrate measurement points (main and
inter-transects):

1. Record presence/absence of **macroalgae** on the substrate particle.
2. Record presence/absence of **macrophytes** (rooted vascular aquatic
   plants; mosses excluded).
3. At main transects, estimate percent cover within a 1 m radius.

### Module G: Bank Stability

At each main transect, for both left and right banks [@ode2016]:

1. Estimate the **percent of bank covered by erosion** (exposed bare
   soil, slumping, undercutting) to the nearest 5%.
2. Estimate the **angle of the bank** (undercut, vertical, steep,
   gradual, flat).

### Module H: Human Influence

At each main transect, record the proximity of human influences within
a 5 m upstream/downstream window and 10 m from each bank. Record each
feature as 0 (absent), P (present > 10 m), C (within 10 m), or B (on
bank). Features include: walls/rip-rap/dams, buildings, pavement,
roads/railroads, pipes, landfill/trash, park/lawn, row crops,
pasture/hay, logging, and mining.

### Module I: Riparian Vegetation

At each main transect, for both left and right banks, estimate areal
cover (0--4 scale: 0 absent, 1 < 10%, 2 = 10--40%, 3 = 40--75%,
4 > 75%) in three layers:

- Canopy (> 5 m)
- Understory (0.5--5 m)
- Ground cover (< 0.5 m)

Record the dominant vegetation type for each layer.

### Module J: Instream Cover

At each main transect, estimate percent cover of instream features
within one channel width upstream and downstream of the transect line:

| Feature | Definition |
|:--------|:-----------|
| Boulder (> 25 cm) | Visual estimate of surface coverage |
| Cobble (6.4--25 cm) | Visual estimate |
| Wood (snag, rootwad) | Visual estimate |
| Overhanging vegetation | Bank overhang within 0.5 m of water surface |
| Undercut bank | Bank extending over water |
| Macroalgae | Attached filamentous or mat-forming algae |
| Macrophytes | Rooted vascular aquatic plants |

### Module L: Channel Slope and Sinuosity

Measure channel slope using a clinometer at a minimum of three
measurement intervals along the reach (between Transects A--C, E--G,
and I--K) or more frequently if slope is variable.

Measure sinuosity by comparing total thalweg length (measured with the
tape along the thalweg) to the straight-line valley distance (measured
with a compass and tape) [@ode2016].

### Module M: Photographs

At each main transect, take the following photographs:

1. Looking upstream along the thalweg
2. Looking downstream along the thalweg
3. Left bank at the transect line
4. Right bank at the transect line

At Transects A and K, also photograph the downstream and upstream reach
boundaries. All photographs should include the transect label (flagging
or field data sheet) in the frame for orientation.

Record photo file names in the field data sheet.


## Quality Control

### Inter-Observer Variability

For substrate measurements, the precision targets are [@ode2016]:

- Median substrate size class (D50): agreement within one Wentworth
  size class between independent observers
- Embeddedness: agreement within 15 percentage points

### Repeat Measurements

For periodic quality assurance, conduct a repeat measurement by an
independent crew within 48 hours. Both crews must achieve agreement
within the precision targets above.

### Common Errors to Avoid

- Measuring transects out of sequence (always work upstream)
- Inconsistent bankfull identification between crew members (calibrate
  at the first transect)
- Forgetting to record GPS coordinates at Transects A and K
- Omitting inter-transect measurements (required for full IPI
  calculation)
- Failing to record the measurement units (mm vs. size class code) for
  substrate

## Training Record

Before conducting physical habitat assessments independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd), and the SWAMP
   Supplemental Guidance Document [@ode2016] in full
2. Review the SWAMP physical habitat field data sheets (Appendix A)
3. Participate in a calibration exercise for bankfull identification
   and substrate measurement with an experienced crew leader
4. Complete at least one full reach assessment under supervision, with
   substrate and embeddedness estimates agreeing with the trainer
   within the precision targets in §9
5. Demonstrate proper densiometer technique and slope measurement
6. Be signed off by the PI or field lead


## Appendix A: Field Data Sheets {.appendix}

SWAMP Bioassessment Field Data Sheets (including physical habitat
forms) are available from
[SWAMP\@waterboards.ca.gov](mailto:SWAMP@waterboards.ca.gov) or at:
<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/swamp/bioassessment/sops.html>

Print on waterproof paper (Rite in the Rain) for field use. Forms
needed:

1. Station Information and Notable Field Conditions
2. Channel/Riparian Cross-Section and Thalweg Profile (one per
   transect)
3. Slope and Bearing
4. Post-Sampling Qualitative Observations
5. Discharge Measurement (if applicable)


## Appendix B: Quick Reference -- Transect Layout {.appendix}

For a 150 m reach (average wetted width ≤ 10 m):

| Transect | Station (m) | Type  |
|:---------|:------------|:------|
| A        | 0           | Main  |
| AB       | 7.5         | Inter |
| B        | 15          | Main  |
| BC       | 22.5        | Inter |
| C        | 30          | Main  |
| ... | ... | ... |
| K        | 150         | Main  |

For a 250 m reach, multiply all station distances by 250/150.


## Appendix C: Substrate Size Class Quick Reference {.appendix}

| Code | Class          | Size Range (mm)    |
|:-----|:---------------|:-------------------|
| RS   | Bedrock smooth | Continuous         |
| RR   | Bedrock rough  | Continuous         |
| HP   | Hardpan        | Continuous         |
| BL   | Boulder        | > 250              |
| CB   | Cobble         | 64--250            |
| GC   | Coarse gravel  | 16--64             |
| GF   | Fine gravel    | 2--16              |
| SA   | Sand           | 0.06--2            |
| FN   | Fines          | < 0.06             |
| WD   | Wood           | --                 |
| OT   | Other          | --                 |

Always measure the **b-axis** (intermediate axis) of the particle.
